name: trips
description: Count of trips that passed every quarantine rule.
warehouse_sql:
select count(*) as trips
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(trips) as trips
from agg

name: revenue
description: Total paid by riders, including tips, tolls and surcharges. For yellow and green this is the published total_amount. For hire vehicle files publish no total, so it is summed from the components, which is stated in docs/data.md and is not the same construction.
warehouse_sql:
select sum(total_amount) as revenue
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(total_amount_sum) as revenue
from agg

name: fare_revenue
description: Base fare only, before tips, tolls and surcharges.
warehouse_sql:
select sum(fare_amount) as fare_revenue
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(fare_amount_sum) as fare_revenue
from agg

name: mean_fare
warehouse_sql:
select avg(fare_amount) as mean_fare
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(fare_amount_sum) / nullif(sum(trips), 0) as mean_fare
from agg

name: mean_distance_mi
warehouse_sql:
select avg(trip_distance) as mean_distance_mi
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(trip_distance_sum) / nullif(sum(trips), 0) as mean_distance_mi
from agg

name: mean_duration_min
warehouse_sql:
select avg(duration_s) / 60.0 as mean_duration_min
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(duration_s_sum) / nullif(sum(trips), 0) / 60.0 as mean_duration_min
from agg

name: mean_speed_mph
description: Total distance over total time, not the mean of per trip speeds. The two differ, and the ratio of sums is the one that answers "how fast does the fleet move", because it weights a forty minute crawl more than a two minute hop. The mean of ratios answers a different question and is the one people compute by accident.
warehouse_sql:
select sum(trip_distance) / nullif(sum(duration_s), 0) * 3600.0 as mean_speed_mph
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(trip_distance_sum) / nullif(sum(duration_s_sum), 0) * 3600.0 as mean_speed_mph
from agg

name: revenue_per_mile
warehouse_sql:
select sum(total_amount) / nullif(sum(trip_distance), 0) as revenue_per_mile
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(total_amount_sum) / nullif(sum(trip_distance_sum), 0) as revenue_per_mile
from agg

name: tip_rate
description: Tips as a share of fare, over trips whose payment channel records a tip. Cash trips record a tip of zero because no tip passed through the meter, and that zero is a missing value. Including them drags this number down by about a third on yellow and green, which is why most published NYC tip rates are wrong. For hire vehicle trips are settled in the app, so their zeroes are real zeroes and they are included.
warehouse_sql:
-- population: tip_is_observable
select sum(case when tip_is_observable then tip_amount end) / nullif(sum(case when tip_is_observable then fare_amount end), 0) as tip_rate
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(tip_obs_tip_sum) / nullif(sum(tip_obs_fare_sum), 0) as tip_rate
from agg

name: tipped_share
description: Share of trips that left any tip at all, over trips whose payment channel records one. This is the proportion that carries a Wilson interval; the tip rate above is a ratio of sums and does not.
warehouse_sql:
-- population: tip_is_observable
select count(*) filter (where tip_is_observable and tip_amount > 0)::double / nullif(count(*) filter (where tip_is_observable), 0) as tipped_share
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(tipped_trips)::double / nullif(sum(tip_obs_trips), 0) as tipped_share
from agg

name: airport_share
description: Share of trips with an airport at either end.
warehouse_sql:
select count(*) filter (where is_airport_trip)::double / nullif(count(*), 0) as airport_share
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(airport_trips)::double / nullif(sum(trips), 0) as airport_share
from agg

name: unknown_zone_share
description: Share of trips with an unresolved zone at either end. Published because these trips are excluded from every geographic aggregate, and a reader needs to know how much of the city is missing from the map.
warehouse_sql:
select count(*) filter (where not has_known_geography)::double / nullif(count(*), 0) as unknown_zone_share
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(unknown_zone_trips)::double / nullif(sum(trips), 0) as unknown_zone_share
from agg

name: card_share
description: Share of yellow and green trips settled by card. For hire vehicle trips are all settled in the app and are excluded, since including them would make this a measure of market share rather than of payment behaviour.
warehouse_sql:
-- population: service in ('yellow', 'green')
select count(*) filter (where payment_type = 'card')::double / nullif(count(*) filter (where service in ('yellow', 'green')), 0) as card_share
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(card_trips)::double / nullif(sum(metered_trips), 0) as card_share
from agg

name: flat_rate_share
description: Share of metered trips on a flat rate, which is the JFK rate and the Newark rate. Visible as horizontal bands in the fare against distance chart, and the reason that chart is not a clean curve.
warehouse_sql:
-- population: ratecode_id in (2, 3)
select count(*) filter (where ratecode_id in (2, 3))::double / nullif(count(*) filter (where service in ('yellow', 'green')), 0) as flat_rate_share
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(flat_rate_trips)::double / nullif(sum(metered_trips), 0) as flat_rate_share
from agg

name: congestion_revenue
description: Total congestion surcharge collected. Null before February 2019 rather than zero, so a window that spans the introduction shows a gap and not a step from nothing.
warehouse_sql:
select sum(congestion_surcharge) as congestion_revenue
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(congestion_surcharge_sum) as congestion_revenue
from agg

name: mean_passengers
description: Mean passengers per trip, over trips that record it. For hire vehicle files do not, and their trips are excluded rather than counted as one.
warehouse_sql:
-- population: passenger_count is not null
select avg(passenger_count) as mean_passengers
from fct_trip
browser_sql:
select sum(passenger_count_sum) / nullif(sum(passenger_trips), 0) as mean_passengers
from agg
